headline: Google fruit fly brain simulation trained to play Balatro with 20% win rate
summary: A Balatro fan claims to have trained a digital fruit fly brain model, mapped by Google, to play the roguelike deck-builder, achieving a 20% success rate.
details: A dedicated Balatro player has reportedly trained a digital fruit fly brain simulation, based on Google's recent mapping of the insect's neural network, to play the popular roguelike deck-builder. The AI model currently achieves a 20% win rate on random seeds.

The user, ActualAerie1011 on Reddit, shared a video demonstrating the simulation playing Balatro on the lowest difficulty (White Stake) with the default Red Deck. This feat follows other creative uses of the fruit fly brain model, including simulating a day trader and teaching it parallel parking.

The training process involved a trainer algorithm that plays a seed alongside the brain model. The model is then rewarded or punished based on its in-game choices, aiming to discover optimal strategies. The user states the AI only has access to on-screen information and that training is ongoing.

While impressive, some users have expressed skepticism due to the limited details provided about the training methodology and the lack of a publicly available project repository. Similar AI projects for Balatro, such as BalatroBot and BalatroLLM, have existed for about a year.

Balatro's complexity, particularly the intricate interactions between various Joker cards and scoring mechanics, makes it a challenging game to master, even for humans. Training an AI to achieve consistency, especially at higher difficulties, presents a significant hurdle.
